title: A multiplicative cover with trivial Picard group
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups below are affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Smoothness and connectedness are as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Write $\operatorname{Pic}(G)$ for the abelian group of isomorphism classes of invertible $\mathcal O_G$-modules, with tensor product as addition; zero is the class of $\mathcal O_G$, and an invertible module is an $\mathcal O_G$-module locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_G$. A multiplicative isogeny is a homomorphism $f:G\to H$ for which $F[H]\to F[G]$ is faithfully flat and whose scheme-theoretic kernel is finite and diagonalizable. Faithfully flat means that extension of scalars is exact and detects zero modules. Finite means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra. Diagonalizable means isomorphic to $D(M)=\operatorname{Spec}F[M]$ for a finite abelian group $M$, where $F[M]$ has basis $e^m$, multiplication $e^me^n=e^{m+n}$, comultiplication $e^m\mapsto e^m\otimes e^m$, counit $e^m\mapsto1$ and antipode $e^m\mapsto e^{-m}$. For every smooth connected group $G$, there exist a smooth connected group $P$ and a multiplicative isogeny $f:P\to G$ such that $\operatorname{Pic}(P)=0$. The trivial group is included.

source.place: Proposition 18.22 (Iversen 1976, 2.7), printed pp.392--393, under the standing split connected group-variety hypothesis (automatic over F); definitions 18.1 and 18.7.

proof.text: Choose a Borel subgroup $B\subseteq G$ and put $Q=G/B$, with quotient $\pi:G\to Q$. By [lem-sfb-borel-characteristic-picard-sequence], $\pi^*:\operatorname{Pic}(Q)\to\operatorname{Pic}(G)$ is onto. By [lem-sfb-flag-effective-picard-generators], choose $\mathcal L_1,\ldots,\mathcal L_r$ generating $\operatorname{Pic}(Q)$, each with nonzero sections. Thus the classes $[\pi^*\mathcal L_i]$ generate $\operatorname{Pic}(G)$.

source.place: Proposition 18.22, first paragraph and diagram, pp.392--393; Lemma 18.21; Theorem 18.15.

proof.text: For each $i$, apply [lem-sfb-flag-projective-linear-system] to $\mathcal L_i$: obtain $V_i=\Gamma(Q,\mathcal L_i)\ne0$, $a_i:G\to\operatorname{PGL}(V_i)$ and an $a_i$-equivariant $t_i:Q\to\mathbf P(V_i)$ with $\mathcal L_i\simeq t_i^*\mathcal O(1)$. Retain the natural linear action of $\operatorname{GL}(V_i)$ on the tautological line.

Induct on $i=0,\ldots,r$. Start with $P_0=G$ and $f_0=\mathrm{id}_G$, which is multiplicative since its coordinate map is the identity and its kernel is $D(0)$. Given the smooth connected $P_{i-1}$ and multiplicative $f_{i-1}:P_{i-1}\to G$, apply [lem-sfb-projective-representation-smooth-lift] to $a_i\circ f_{i-1}$. It gives a smooth connected $P_i$, a multiplicative $q_i:P_i\to P_{i-1}$ and $\rho_i:P_i\to\operatorname{SL}(V_i)$ whose projectivization is $a_i f_{i-1}q_i$. Set $f_i=f_{i-1}q_i$. It is multiplicative by [lem-sfb-multiplicative-isogeny-composition]. This induction constructs all $P_i,f_i,\rho_i$, without assuming that the raw fibre product is smooth or connected.

source.place: Proposition 18.22, final paragraph, p.393, applied successively to the finite list; Proposition 18.2, p.387; reduced-component correction from 18.6(a), p.388.

proof.text: At stage $i$, put $y_i=t_i(eB)$ and let $W_i=\mathcal O(1)|_{y_i}$, a one-dimensional $F$-vector space. Equivariance gives $t_i\pi f_i(p)=\overline{\rho_i(p)}y_i$. The tautological linear action from [lem-sfb-flag-projective-linear-system] therefore defines an isomorphism from $P_i\times_F W_i$ onto the line bundle $f_i^*\pi^*\mathcal L_i$: on fibres it sends $(p,w)$ to $(p,\rho_i(p)w)$, with inverse $(p,z)\mapsto(p,\rho_i(p)^{-1}z)$. These are regular scheme maps and mutually inverse after every scalar extension. A nonzero basis of $W_i$ trivializes this bundle. For $j<i$, a trivialization on $P_{i-1}$ remains a trivialization after pullback along $q_i$, since $f_i^*\pi^*\mathcal L_j=q_i^*f_{i-1}^*\pi^*\mathcal L_j$. Induction proves that $f_r^*$ kills every generator $[\pi^*\mathcal L_i]$.

source.place: Proposition 18.22, homogeneous-line argument, p.393; explicit trivialization on the group, using 18.10 and 18.12--18.13.

proof.text: Put $P=P_r$ and $f=f_r$. Step 4 and generation in step 1 show $f^*:\operatorname{Pic}(G)\to\operatorname{Pic}(P)$ is zero: apply the homomorphism to an integer linear combination of the generators. By [lem-sfb-character-picard-isogeny-sequence], $f^*$ is also surjective, since $f$ is a multiplicative isogeny of smooth connected affine groups. Thus every element of $\operatorname{Pic}(P)$ is the image of an element of $\operatorname{Pic}(G)$ and is zero. If $r=0$, the construction gives $P=G$, $f=\mathrm{id}$ and the same argument applies. In particular the proof includes the trivial group.

source.place: Proposition 18.22, first sentence of proof, p.392; final surjection in Proposition 18.18 (129), p.391.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 18.22, pp.392--393, with the finite iteration and tautological-line trivialization written explicitly, and the reduced identity-component correction from 18.6(a).
